history.summary: PROBABLE DUPLICATE of seq 801 / Mata Mansa Devi Temple (id mansa-devi-temple-panchkula): this CSV row carries the same name and the same corrected location, so it almost certainly refers to the same shrine rather than a distinct temple. The famous Mata Mansa Devi Temple is NOT in Chandigarh - it stands at Mansa Devi Complex, MDC Sector 4, Panchkula, Haryana (Bilaspur village, Shivalik foothills), about 7-12 km from Chandigarh (CSV state 'Haryana' is correct; CSV town 'Chandigarh' is wrong). The main temple was built 1811-1815 by Maharaja Gopal Das Singh of Mani Majra; 200 metres away is the Patiala Shivalaya built 1840 by Karam Singh, Maharaja of Patiala. The goddess is worshipped in pindi (pebble) form together with Lakshmi and Saraswati; a marble idol is also enshrined. The complex spreads over about 100 acres and is regarded as a Shakti Peeth (Sati's forehead is believed to have fallen here). Managed by the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board.

name: Mata Mansa Devi Temple
town: Panchkula (CSV town 'Chandigarh' is incorrect; the temple is ~7-12 km from Chandigarh)
town_description: Panchkula is a planned city in Haryana adjoining Chandigarh and Mohali (the Tricity), set at the foot of the Shivalik hills. The Mansa Devi temple complex at MDC Sector 4 is one of the Tricity's premier pilgrimage sites, drawing devotees from Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, especially during the twice-yearly Navratri melas.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport (Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport) - about 18-20 km (verify).
travel.railway: Chandigarh Railway Station - about 7 km (verify); autos and taxis readily available.
travel.road: At Mansa Devi Complex, MDC Sector 4/5, off the Ambala-Chandigarh highway; well signposted. Shared autos, private cabs and special buses run from Panchkula and Chandigarh terminals (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri periods (March-April and September-October) are the most vibrant but very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 4:00 AM-10:00 PM daily (verify - one source says 5:00 AM-9:00 PM; hours vary on special occasions). Free entry; footwear not allowed inside; photography restricted.
